 19 Nov 2026 
 RM640mil to ensure water supply reliability in Labuan 
Izham says the water levels at dams are being closely monitored. 
 WATER supply and demand in Selangor have remained stable despite the transboundary haze and warmer weather associated with the El Nino phenomenon earlier this year.
 State infrastructure and agriculture committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said consumption data up to September showed no significant deviation from projections made at the beginning of the year.
 “There are no indications that the haze and El Nino phenomenon have affected water usage.
 “The situation is being closely monitored. No dams have recorded water levels below 80% as of September,” he said during the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting at Bangunan Dewan Negeri Selangor in Shah Alam yesterday.
 He said the state had treated water production capacity of 6,500 million litres per day (MLD), exceeding current demand of 5,370 MLD.
 He was replying to Pang Sock Tao (PH-Kuala Kubu Baharu), who asked how the state government planned to manage water demand amid the haze and warmer weather.
 Pang also sought details on contingency measures by Selangor Water Management Authority (LUAS) and the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) to address potential surges in demand.
 Izham said the state worked closely with LUAS, Air Selangor and DID to monitor dam levels and ensure adequate water supply.
 “Contingency measures include activating reserve pumps in Bestari Jaya and drawing additional water from ponds under the state’s water storage scheme,” he said.
 “We have also identified 20 ponds as alternative water sources and are in the midst of identifying another 140.
 “Together, these ponds have an estimated combined capacity of 160 million cubic metres of water. Research is also being conducted to identify groundwater resources with a potential capacity of 3,200 MLD,” he said.
